Feature 227 — budget (ms) for the shared `BatchGetLatestPrice` singleflight closure, which runs on a context **detached** from the first caller's cancellation/deadline (`context.WithoutCancel`) so coalesced waiters are not cancelled by it; symbols not fetched within it are omitted (never fabricated) and every dropped error is logged as a WARN. Read live per call; `value_type` must be `int` (any other type reads as the default); `≤ 0` or no config watcher → `2500`. Unseeded (feature 227 seeding waiver); SetConfig-bounded `[500,2500]`.

Feature 229 — budget (ms) for the detached `GetLatestQuotes` cold-fetch singleflight closure (`context.WithoutCancel`, so a cancelled first caller never fails coalesced waiters). On a cold failure/timeout the call returns the warm subset, cold symbols omitted (never zero-filled), with a WARN `GetLatestQuotes: cold fetch failed`. Read live per call; `≤ 0` or no watcher → `2500`. Must stay, together with `marketdata.quotes.mark_timeout_ms` (bound = max of the two), below `portfolio.marketdata.quote_timeout_ms` minus the warm read. Unseeded; SetConfig-bounded `[500,5000]`.

Feature 229 — recency window (hours) of both cached quote readers (`GetLatestQuote`, `GetLatestQuotesBatch`: `time >= now − window`, so TimescaleDB excludes older chunks at plan time) and of the cache-age guard (a quote older than the window is returned but never cached). A symbol with no in-window row is cold and fetched live. 7 days covers 3-day weekends + holidays. Read live per call; `≤ 0` or no watcher → `168`. Unseeded (feature 227 D2-style waiver); SetConfig-bounded `[24,720]`.

Feature 231 — max age (hours) of the stored `1d` close usable as a mark; an older (or absent) close leaves `mark_price` unset (never fabricated). Read live per call; `≤ 0` or no watcher → `168`. Unseeded; SetConfig-bounded `[120,720]`.

Feature 231 — per-caller budget (ms) for the `GetLatestQuotes` stored-close lookup that backs `Quote.mark_price` for returned quotes lacking a positive bid and ask (a symbol with no quote at all is still omitted); it runs concurrently with the cold fetch, and on timeout/error those symbols return without `mark_price` and a WARN `GetLatestQuotes: mark lookup failed`. Read live per call; `≤ 0` or no watcher → `500`. Unseeded; SetConfig-bounded `[100,2500]`.

Feature 229 — quote retention (days), enforced by `StartQuoteRetention` (app-level `drop_chunks`; DO's Apache-edition TimescaleDB has no `add_retention_policy`). Read live each hourly run; `≤ 0` or no watcher → `90`, never clamped — a run is **skipped with a WARN** when `days*24 <= marketdata.quotes.latest_lookback_hours` (so it never drops rows the windowed reads serve). Unseeded; SetConfig-bounded `[31,3650]`. See § Quote retention.

Interval for the always-on bar ingester that upserts recent bars for every queried symbol into `marketdata.ohlcv`. Read live each cycle; `0`/negative pauses it. Default 5m (feature 140): with continuous **daily** ingestion, the forming daily bar needn't refresh every 60s — the UI's 5-min chart poll and `GetBars`' staleness fallback additionally cover freshness.

Lookback window the always-on ingester re-fetches each cycle. Overlap is harmless because inserts upsert, and a window wider than the interval lets the feed self-heal after a pause/restart. This raw value (15min) is far too short for the `1d` default — but `ingestRecentBars` widens each timeframe's own window to at least 2× that timeframe's interval (`minIngestLookback`), so `1d` always looks back ≥48h regardless of this key's value.

Bar timeframe(s) the always-on ingester fetches each cycle. A comma-separated list mechanism (not a single value), parsed by the count-agnostic `resolveIngestTimeframes` — feature 143 narrowed the *default* from `15m,1d` to `1d` (feature 140 flipped the platform to daily) because `GetBars`/`BackfillBars` now reject any non-`1d` request, so continuously ingesting 15m served no consumer. Continuous `1d` ingestion keeps daily bars fresh. Each entry is canonicalized through `internal/timeframe`; an unresolvable entry is skipped with a WARN (not a whole-list fallback), and an empty/wholly-unresolvable value falls back to the default. To pause ingestion, use `bar_ingest_interval_ms <= 0` — never a bogus timeframe value.

Interval for `StartOrderIntentSweeper`, the proactive reclaim loop that transitions orphaned `PENDING` intents to `UNKNOWN` after an unattended crash (no retry needed). Matches `trading.fill_poller.interval_ms`'s existing default.
Interval for the broker position/balance sync poller (`syncPositions`). Read live on every cycle.
Consecutive ticks a mismatch must persist before it's a real finding (not a benign propagation delay).

Cooldown between `reconcileTick` broker polls (`ListOrders`/`GetPositions`) for an **already-halted** account — slower than the ordinary `interval_ms` cadence, since a halted account can't place new orders regardless (`isAccountHalted` gates `PlaceOrder`/`ReplaceOrder`) and only needs occasional re-observation to notice broker-side drift (e.g. a manual dashboard order). Read live on every cycle; `<= 0` disables the throttle (polls every tick, matching `interval_ms`'s own convention).
Interval for the broker-state-reconciliation poller (`reconcileTick`). Read live on every cycle.
